entities.summary: Fan Chengda, courtesy name Zhineng (致能), was a Chinese geographer, poet, and politician. One of the best-known Chinese poets of the Song Dynasty, he served as a government official, and was an academic authority in geography, especially the southern provinces of China. His written work also falls under the literary category of 'travel record literature', a narrative and prose style approach to writing about one's travel experiences, which was popular in China during the Song Dynasty. He, along with Yang Wanli, Lu You, and You Mao, are considered to be the "four masters" of Southern Song dynasty poetry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the 'four masters' of Southern Song dynasty poetry, Fan Chengda's written work had a significant regional impact on Chinese literature and geography during the Song Dynasty. His travel record literature style influenced later generations of poets.
